Hi all —

Following up with the engineering answers. I'll focus on the request/response schema and streaming semantics you asked about. Short answers first, details after.

Summary answers:
- Chat vs completions: Use the chat endpoint for multi-turn stateful interactions (the SDK manages message roles & KV cache). Use completions for single-turn prompts. Chat includes role metadata which helps structured tool calling.
- Tokenization & max_tokens: The SDK exposes a tokenizer util. max_tokens governs the response-side token budget; requests are truncated from the left if the total (prompt + max_tokens) exceeds the model limit. We recommend reserving ~25% of the model context for generation to avoid truncation of important prompt context.
- Stop sequences: The SDK supports stop as a list of strings; partial matches will stop generation when any sequence is emitted. For chat, you can also return a structured finish_reason to detect tool-call boundaries.
- Streaming: Streaming returns partial data frames over a persistent connection (SDK supports SSE and WebSocket). Tool-calling and function-calling events may arrive as structured frames — the SDK will emit an onEvent callback for tool_invocation/tool_response.

Example request shapes (pseudo-JSON shown inline in email):

- Chat request (recommended for multi-turn + tool calling):
{ role: "user", content: "Summarize the following: ..." }
Optional: { tools: ["reranker", "kb_search"] }

- Completions request (single-shot):
{ prompt: "Write a short email to a customer about delay...", max_tokens: 150, stop: ["\n\n"] }

Tokenization notes:
- We can run the prompts you send through our token estimator and return a per-prompt token count to help set max_tokens.
- For embeddings + rerankers: embeddings use a separate endpoint; we recommend normalizing text (NFKC) and passing full text for dense embeddings. Reranker workflows typically do: embed(query) -> embed(candidates) -> dot-product / cross-encoder; we can provide a sample reranking microservice.

Auth guidance (short):
- PoC: API key scoped to project + short TTL.
- Production: Recommend mTLS (if using Redwood Private) or customer-managed keys via KMS with request-level signatures for hosted dedicated setups.

I'll paste a sample streaming handler and a chat-to-tool mapping in the follow-up message. Happy to jump on a quick call to demo streaming frames.

Hi Susan / Mark —

Couple of pragmatic configs based on typical Acme-esque latency/cost tradeoffs:

1) Routing example (policy-based):
- header: "x-redwood-priority" = "low_latency" routes to gptx-lt (lower token costs, <50ms p50)
- header: "x-redwood-priority" = "high_quality" routes to gptx-hq (higher cost, better coherence)
- fallback: if target pool is saturated, route to nearest compatible quantized variant with degraded QoS but preserved safety filters.

Config snippet (YAML):
routing: [ {matcher: "header.x-redwood-priority=low_latency", pool: "gptx-lt"}, {matcher: "header.x-redwood-priority=high_quality", pool: "gptx-hq"} ]

2) Auth for production:
- If you deploy Redwood Private in your VPC: enable mTLS + customer KMS for key rotation.
- If you use Redwood Dedicated (hosted): recommend scoped API keys + IP allow-listing + request signing for high-risk operations.

3) Structured output & tool calling:
- Use the chat endpoint and declare tools in the request. The runtime will return a tool_call event frame during streaming or a tool_call object at completion.
- We recommend a JSON-schema field in your prompt for structured output. Our SDK has a validator that will enforce the schema and will return a parse_error code if validation fails.

Files & links: Attached the same SDK guide (quickstart) and a network diagram. Also attaching a short Playbook (Drive link) that walks through embedding + reranker integration patterns.

Proposed next step: 30-min engineering demo where we: run a sample prompt through token estimator, show a streaming session with tool-calling, and sketch routing configs. Availability: Tue/Wed next week 10-12 PST.

Regards,
David Kim

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our infra/dev team: 

1) For stop sequences: if we pass multiple stop strings, do you stop at the first match globally or per-choice? Also, does streaming send a final frame when stop is triggered?
2) If we use chat with a tool-call, how does the SDK indicate that the tool was invoked vs. the model generating text? We need a deterministic marker so our downstream pipeline can trigger the external retriever.
3) Embedding size: what are the vector dims for the recommended embedding model? We plan to store embeddings in our vector DB and want to confirm index sizing.

We can do the 30-min demo — Tue 2026-03-24 at 10:30 PST works for our team. Please confirm.

Hi Susan — quick answers inline: 

1) Stop sequences: we stop at the first emitted sequence globally (across choices). Streaming: yes — we emit a final control frame finish_reason="stop_sequence" and then close the stream. Your handler will receive that final frame so you can finalize downstream processing.

2) Tool-call indication: the SDK emits explicit event types. Example frames: {type:"content", data:"..."}, {type:"tool_call", tool:"kb_search", args:{...}}, {type:"tool_response", tool:"kb_search", result:{...}}. The chat completion response will also include a top-level finish_reason and, for non-stream flows, a tool_call object. This is deterministic for triggering the retriever.

3) Embedding dims: recommended model currently returns 1536-d vectors. We can also offer 768-d low-cost vectors for high-volume use cases. We'll share an estimate for storage given your expected corpus size if you provide approximate doc counts.

I'll add these items to the demo agenda and prepare a short token-estimation script to run on your sample prompts (if you share them ahead of time). Confirmed: Tue 2026-03-24 10:30 PST — I'll send a calendar invite.
